_description: Radiation calibration dataset for Lunar Habitat AI Radiation Model V1
_provenance_note: Dose values and incident GCR flux reductions are directly reported by Burahmah & Heilbronn (2023) PHITS simulations. Dose conversions from uSv/day to mSv/year are calculated. No SVF value is claimed to be measured by the source paper. The model uses a terrain-shielding proxy derived from the regional SVF: shielding_proxy = 1 - SVF.

calibration_points.notes: Published open-surface reference. Shielding proxy is zero by definition.

solar_maximum_scenarios.reason: V1 defaults to solar minimum (GCR maximum, worst-case for long-duration exposure). Solar maximum scenarios from the same paper (open surface 260.8 uSv/day, deep wall 142.4 uSv/day) are excluded to avoid mixing solar conditions.

naito_2023_neutron_gamma.reason: Naito, Kusano & Kodaira (2023) DOI 10.1038/s41598-023-40405-0 reports neutron and gamma-ray AMBIENT DOSE EQUIVALENT (H*(10)), not effective dose equivalent. These are physically incompatible quantities and cannot be mixed with the Burahmah & Heilbronn effective dose values without conversion factors that depend on geometry and particle field. Used as background literature only.
naito_2023_neutron_gamma.naito_effective_dose_note: Naito et al. also report 420 mSv/year as a worst-case effective dose for the lunar surface (solar minimum). This is consistent with BH2023 (762.1 uSv/day = 278 mSv/year is lower — the ~420 mSv/year may include different GCR model or shielding assumptions). Due to inability to verify exact physical quantity compatibility, Naito effective dose is noted as supporting context but not used as a calibration anchor.

metadata.primary_source: Burahmah & Heilbronn (2023), Comparison of Doses in Lunar Habitats Located at the Surface and in Crater, Aerospace 10(11), 970
metadata.important_limitation: The published paper does not report SVF. Its incident GCR flux reduction values are used as calibration evidence for the terrain-shielding proxy. The mapping from regional SVF to incident GCR shielding is therefore a first-order approximation.
metadata.independent_validation: Not available because all five calibration points come from the same PHITS study.
